findings.suggested_fix: Mark T-1/T-5 as accepted residual risk until sign-in lands, and add a non-blocking question asking the stage approver to accept that risk explicitly.
findings.text: T-1 and T-5 call identify/requirePermission an existing mitigation. C3, cited by the same artifact, says every request is staff and every permission is granted, so in the MVP there is no effective access control. This is accepted residual risk, not a mitigation.

findings.text: T-6 cites C7 for 'the new data inherits the patient read permission'. C7 only says a GET route exists and says nothing about which permission it declares.

findings.text: Threats are listed in component order, not by risk. The rubric's top clarity score asks for risk ordering.

questions.text: Until sign-in replaces identify/requirePermission, any caller can read patient pages and the new visit counts. Do you accept this as residual risk for HMS-5?

rubric_items.reason: All seven design components have at least one threat. Personal-data handlers (PatientDetailPage, PatientService, PatientRepo, AppointmentRepo) are all covered.
Most threats are specific to the visit_summary change (echo in PATCH, wrong-id join, aggregate cost). T-2 (markup injection of integers) and T-9 are fairly generic.

Mitigations are either cited existing controls or clearly labelled new controls. T-1, T-5 and T-6 rely on identity checks that C3 says grant everything in the MVP, and a few cites (C7 in T-6, C8 in T-3) do not prove the stated point.
The index gap is asked as Q-01. The MVP no-op auth residual risk is presented as mitigated, not asked. The design's open Q-01/Q-02, which assumed REQ-2/3/9 depend on, are not carried over.
Readable, consistent component-by-component layout with a matching prose summary. Threats are ordered by component, not by risk.
